label: The apply flow is fail-closed and staged: validate all; if --apply and any packet unreadable, write nothing and exit 2; repair only non-archived failing packets; re-validate; record remaining findings only for packets already failing at the start.

Recorded findings live in upgrade-baseline.json beside the packet's documents, written atomically as {schema, recordedBy, recordedAt, findings:[{rule, detail}]}; the write refuses to leave the roots and an identical set returns unchanged, making re-record idempotent.

The validator reads the baseline: a listed finding is relaxed to a warning with a recorded note; an unlisted one stays an error; every copy of a repeated detail must be listed or the entry flips back to an error.

The never-recorded set is the derivable class: GENERATED_METADATA_INTEGRITY, GENERATED_METADATA_DRIFT, METADATA_DISK_PATH_CONSISTENCY, CANONICAL_SAVE_LINEAGE_REQUIRED, GRAPH_METADATA_CHILD_IDENTITY; for live packets these can never become warnings and must be repaired, while archived packets are exempt from the filter.
Damage protection is built in: a packet that passed before a repair step and fails after it is never recorded, so pipeline-caused regressions stay errors instead of being hidden.

Archived packets are recorded only, never repaired, unless --include-archive is passed deliberately; their findings can still be recorded because recording writes the baseline beside the packet without touching its documents.

Reversibility follows from the writes: dry default, structure/derived/path-only repairs with refusal boundaries, all edits in tracked files so git restores them, and deleting a baseline entry re-raises its error rather than losing it. (INFERRED as a documented operator contract; no operator-facing baseline lifecycle doc was found.)
